description:
PLANNING / AGREEMENT REQUIRED — user direction 2026-11-26 supersedes the earlier implementation claim. Keep this issue in progress. The current uncommitted all-not_applicable native-Web patch is incomplete and must not be treated as delivering configurable BO-chat settings. Preserve it for review; replace it only after agreement on this plan. No further production/test code edits, commits, pushes or publication are authorized by this planning turn.

Scope: native BO chat configuration and its integration contract with the downstream delivery stack. WebWidget external source/integration remains separately tracked in zaq-h2i.4.2; it is not a blocker for independent native-Web configuration.

Live audit:
- feat/channel-file-settings bfb3e677c owns shared normalization, FileSettings/Ecto, resolver, Advanced components and authoritative proposed-save validation.
- ../zaq-feat-delivery_plan is clean at 6d94a2813, equal to updated dark-theme. It contains no delivery-specific commits yet. Do not claim native-Web file transport is already implemented there.
- Reference ../zaq-feat-channel-files at 8d987fa5 has Channels.Delivery.Attachments.build_plan/3, Executor and an Outgoing.delivery selection contract, integrated for Jido/SMTP. Channels.Api.delivery_connection/3 explicitly selects nil config for native web. WebBridge has no transport_requirements/2, prepare_delivery_message/3 or execute_delivery_step/3 integration. Do not copy the full PR6 stack or its dependency pins.
- Native ChatLive.run_pipeline_async uses Delivery.bo/1 and BridgeClient with no persisted connector. ChannelConfig excludes provider web. Existing native delivery only projects text/tool response payloads.
- Native BO already has authenticated FileController.show_ref, PreviewReference.sign_record/2 and FilePreviewData.load_raw with current-user authorization/materialization. These are candidates for native attachment links; their coverage of supported Record kinds and history refresh must be tested, not assumed complete.

PROPOSED OWNER (pending agreement):
Zaq.System owns one global JSON value in the existing system_configs table at system.communication.web.file_delivery. Store the existing normalized FileSettings map (integer bytes/count plus send_on_file_failure). This is installation-wide, not per user/conversation/agent or a WebWidget connector. No new table, persisted ChannelConfig row, synthetic adapter or new production module. Missing settings retain existing text-chat behavior; unknown capacity never becomes unlimited. Existing System.Config unique key and transaction/upsert machinery own persistence.

REUSE / MISSING-CONTRACT EVIDENCE:
- Extend System's existing configuration ownership and System.Config changesets/transaction helpers. Reuse FileSettings.merge_form, validate/validate_changeset, add_errors/errors and exact MB conversion; do not add an embedded schema or validator.
- Existing SaveEmailConnector and ManageWidgetConnector are scoped to exact email/widget identities; ManageLiveUpdateSettings owns connector/live-update operations. None is a semantically correct native global settings save. Do not force BO-chat settings through an unrelated Action.
- Necessary plan amendment: add native-Web get/save clauses to the existing Engine.Api system_config event family (proposed names system_config_get_native_web_file_settings and system_config_save_native_web_file_settings), with confidential events and explicit BOActor.current_user management authorization. System methods own business logic; existing Repo transaction and Config changeset perform the write. This is a local administrative configuration operation, not a new agent/workflow tool or Action module. Runtime reads must preserve trusted execution-actor boundaries separately from management authorization; nil identity is never elevated permission.
- Existing :channel_capability_snapshot scope:proposal only accepts ChannelConfig structs. Extend that same boundary with a narrowly validated native-Web proposal representation prepared by Engine from the singleton key: fixed provider web, no connector/config ID, no user-selected storage key, file_delivery settings only. Preserve all existing ChannelConfig identity checks. Do not fabricate a persisted ChannelConfig identity or add a snapshot API. System validates the final normalized proposed value through this same event immediately before its atomic write, never a BO cached/stored-only snapshot.

DECLARATION / DELIVERY CONTRACT:
Web.Delivery is the candidate existing native delivery owner; extend it with a pure native configuration declaration projection, consumed by WebBridge.capability_snapshot/1. CommunicationBridge remains the only metadata normalizer. Define per-file max_attachment_bytes as unresolved/configurable/optional and max_attachments_per_message as unresolved/configurable/required when file support is usable; both integer, bytes/count, greater_than 0. Only expose other existing fields where the agreed native transport can enforce them. Encoded/upload limits stay unresolved unless the actual native transport proves inapplicability; do not mark all limits not_applicable. Values do not come from configured overrides and are not invented ceilings. Failure policy stays in stored settings.
Proposed native transport for the downstream delivery PR: publish authorized attachment references alongside the answer through existing Web.Response/ChatLive live/history paths and authenticated BO file serving, reusing the shared delivery planner and TransportRequirements.resolve/2 once per attempt. Direct attachment publication maps to existing send_with_attachments only if execution semantics fit; no new transfer mode or framework. Reuse existing materialization and permission boundaries; do not ship browser-visible bytes/paths/credentials or bypass authorization. Verify actual sizes/counts and failure policy in native delivery tests. Current support statuses remain truthful and unchanged until native delivery is actually implemented/tested; configuration metadata must not enable support. Required fields apply only when associated support is usable. The downstream planner must consume the same selected native settings projection used by persistence; no second settings store, provider-specific resolver, or read from the BO form cache.

BO PLACEMENT (pending agreement): existing SystemConfigLive GlobalTab gains a BO chat settings section using ConnectionSettings.editor and FileDeliverySettings in Advanced. No new LiveView/component/module. Load through Engine, validate from cached assigns, Save through the authoritative Engine operation, retain drafts/errors on failure and keep Cancel read-only. Keep file errors on their existing fields. Update existing Storybook stories and existing UX/E2E scenario owners rather than creating another UI approval/E2E framework.

TESTS / ACCEPTANCE:
Write original tests before implementation for singleton persistence, no fabricated channel rows/IDs, exact-byte save/reload, optional blank/whitespace clearing, positive/integer validation and applicable required rejection, proposal vs cached facts, final-state validation and atomic rollback, concurrent/selected scope isolation from widgets, actor/confidentiality rejection, declaration purity, and Advanced draft/error behavior. Extend existing System/Engine/Bridge/FileSettings/LiveView suites. Preserve committed assertions/statuses/defaults/SMTP behavior; changes to existing test behavior require explicit approval. Native live/history/download tests belong to downstream file-delivery work and must prove truthful support before advertising it. Follow issue mix q/focused checks and existing human UX → new E2E → coverage/final precommit gates; no self-approval or duplicate gates.

AGREEMENT NEEDED: approve the system-wide System/config key owner (versus introducing a native ChannelConfig), existing SystemConfig Global/BO chat UI placement, and the two concrete Engine/proposal-boundary extensions above. Until then, no implementation continuation. Beadwork owns the plan; repository diff remains unchanged from the incomplete implementation.

comments.text: Live audit: working in requested existing feat/channel-file-settings at bfb3e677c; worktree clean. PR_STACK.md is absent from all four relevant worktree roots, so verified live ancestry directly (capabilities → settings → dark-theme → delivery_plan). No branch/history edits planned. Action reuse assessment: extend existing WebBridge.capability_snapshot/1 built-in native-Web declaration, reuse Bridge.capability_snapshot normalization/event, CommunicationBridge.normalize_capability_snapshot/2, FileSettings, resolver and authorized persistence owners unchanged. Web.Delivery is a validated delivery-descriptor owner (bo/1, events/new/reference), not a configuration declaration API; Response and final_payload/send_reply confirm no attachment sending. Keep metadata beside the existing native profile rather than add an unnecessary public accessor or file-specific callback. Native file limits will be fixed/not_applicable, typed bytes/count, required false; transfer mode unresolved and attachment edits false. Current WebWidget.HostAdapter at locked 42b7ef71 exposes only infrastructure/runtime/ingress/installation APIs, with no capabilities or file declarations; preserve its unresolved metadata and current support meanings. No new API/module/Action/UI/validator/dependency changes. Add original tests only for producer purity, native vs widget semantics, shared controls and persistence rejection/rollback; usable-file required/positive/bounds cases remain covered by existing foundation tests and cannot be claimed as native-Web support.

Additional boundary evidence: ChannelConfig @valid_providers excludes native web; BO ChatLive supplies a configless Delivery.bo/1 descriptor. Native Web has no persisted connector/Advanced form to wire. Do not add one for metadata. Native declarations will be proven through the real Bridge normalization and existing shared component/validator/resolver. Existing configured widget persistence will be regression-tested using production WebBridge, remaining unsupported/unresolved until external declarations exist. No valid native file override or usable-file required-field path exists to test truthfully. This subset is an explicit external-source limitation, not permission to invent support.

Implementation evidence: five native-Web limits now explicitly fixed/not_applicable with integer bytes/count metadata; transfer mode unresolved and attachment edits false. All existing support statuses remain intact. Added producer/envelope, shared component, no-settings-derived-ceilings property and production WidgetConnectorSettings atomic rollback/selected-config/blank-save regressions; no existing test lines removed or behavioral assertions changed. TDD: producer + component tests failed before implementation (18/21 passed) in /tmp/zaq-h2i-4-1-red.log; focused post-fix 21 passed (1 property) plus widget suite 20 passed (1 property). mix q initially reported two new-test alias suggestions; code-quality skill applied local aliases only and rerun passed (/tmp/zaq-h2i-4-1-q.log). Broader regressions running. Added dependency .4.2 → .4.1 for remaining WebWidget integration; do not close this issue as fully complete.

Final issue-level validation: 678 passed (17 properties, 661 tests), /tmp/zaq-h2i-4-1-regression.log. Includes production Web delivery/adapter suites, Channels API/shared normalization/SMTP, resolver, FileSettings, ChannelConfig final-preparation rollback, grouped policy/widget/email persistence, shared controls and widget/SMTP LiveViews. mix q passed; git diff --check passed. Existing assertions preserved; no new production module/helper/API/UI/save path or dependency changes. No browser suite rerun: no rendered route or UI implementation changed (native Web has no persisted settings route); existing component/LiveView suites passed, and existing feature UX/new-E2E/coverage/final precommit gates remain in their owners. Native subset is ready for review; remaining WebWidget subset genuinely depends on external source .4.2, so .4.1 remains in progress with that blocker. No commits, pushes or publication performed.
